etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French complication, from Latin complicatio, complicationem. Morphologically complicate +‎ -ion

definitions.definition: The act or process of complicating.
The state of being complicated; intricate or confused relation of parts; complexity.
A person who doesn't fit in with the main scheme of things; an interloper.
(medicine) A disease or diseases, or adventitious circumstances or conditions, coexistent with and modifying a primary disease, but not necessarily connected with it.
(horology) A feature beyond basic time display in a timepiece.

quote.citation: 2013, Stacy Perman, A Grand Complication: The Race to Build the World's Most Legendary Watch, Simon and Schuster, →ISBN, page 35:
quote.text: Obsessed, he was after a watch that contained the greatest number of complications in the boldest combinations in the smallest space imaginable.

quote.citation: 2023 May 28, Brian Ng, “Is one of these students the next Breguet?”, in FT Weekend, HTSI, page 43:
quote.text: In their final year, each student must make their own watch with a complication—from a tourbillon to a chiming mode to having a date display.
the snaky complication in the Caduceus or rod of Hermes.
